question: A writer wants one rule to apply everywhere she uses Claude, and a second rule to apply only inside one client Project. Which two placements are correct? Select two.
options: A) Put both of the rules into the client Project's instructions, since those apply account-wide.
B) Put the client-specific rule into that Project's instructions so it applies only inside it.
C) Put the everywhere rule into her account-wide personalization settings so it always applies.
D) Put both rules at the top of each new chat, since durable settings are for administrators.
E) Put the client rule into her account-wide settings too, so that it is never once missed.
correct_answers: B) Put the client-specific rule into that Project's instructions so it applies only inside it.
C) Put the everywhere rule into her account-wide personalization settings so it always applies.
explanations: Incorrect. Project instructions apply inside that Project only, so putting the global rule there would not apply it everywhere.
Correct. Project instructions are scoped to their Project, which is exactly the boundary the second rule needs.
Correct. Account-wide personalization is the right home for direction that should apply across all of her Claude use.
Incorrect. Durable instruction settings are available to ordinary users, and re-typing rules per chat is what they replace.
Incorrect. Account-wide settings apply to all her work, so a client-specific rule placed there would leak into unrelated chats.
